decisions.reason: As a core next-generation printer highlighted on the homepage, Product A likely met or stayed near aspiration levels and fits the firm's strong hardware, ink and service capabilities in a growing market.

Product B extends the installed base with variable-data software for secure numbering, and its continued mention after launch suggests performance acceptable enough to retain under the firm's digitalization and traceability goals.

Because Product C addresses a practical coding need on non-absorbent surfaces within the firm's established competence set, management would likely keep it as a complementary niche offer despite only moderate visibility.

As a successor app that broadens code decoding and supports end-to-end traceability, Product D is close enough to the core offer that a growing firm with organizational slack would keep it while its ecosystem value remains uncertain.

Inline code verification directly supports compliance and traceability, so even with limited website prominence Product E is strategically important enough to keep as part of a one-stop solution portfolio.
A print layout design software complements the firm's marking systems and common-operation logic, and homepage placement at launch indicates results likely above the threshold needed to continue it.
